name: Nigerian Jollof Rice
description: Jollof rice depends on a real fried-down tomato-pepper base and real long-grain parboiled rice - not basmati, which cooks too soft and doesn't hold up to the technique. Maggi or Knorr cubes are the everyday Nigerian seasoning behind the savory depth here, not an optional extra, and ginger belongs in the base alongside the tomato and pepper.

ingredients_full.note: half for the base, half sliced

ingredients_full.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

ingredients.note: half for the base, half sliced

ingredients.ingredient: Rice, white, long-grain, parboiled, enriched, dry

steps_detailed: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, jalapeño, ginger, and half the onion into a smooth puree.
Brown the chicken in the oil, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the remaining sliced onion in the same oil, 3-4 minutes, then add the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes to deepen its color.
Add the blended puree and simmer uncovered 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it reduces and darkens - this step is what gives jollof its real depth, not a shortcut to skip.
Stir in the rice, coating every grain in the sauce, then add the broth, bay leaf, bouillon, thyme, and chicken.
Cover and cook on low heat 20-25 minutes without stirring, until the rice is tender and the bottom develops a faint char - the prized 'party jollof' crust.
Rest 5 minutes before fluffing and serving.

name: Nigerian Egusi Soup
description: Egusi soup depends on real palm oil, not a neutral substitute - the oil's own color and flavor are part of the dish. Real ground crayfish is the other backbone ingredient here, adding an umami depth that plain stock can't replicate, and the egusi itself is fried in the hot oil in spoonfuls to build the soup's characteristic lumpy texture.

ingredients_full.note: standing in for ugu/fluted pumpkin leaves

ingredients_full.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

ingredients.note: standing in for ugu/fluted pumpkin leaves

ingredients.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.
Mix the ground egusi with a few tablespoons of water into a thick paste.

Heat the palm oil until it shimmers and fry spoonfuls of the egusi paste, breaking them into small lumps, 5-6 minutes, until they turn slightly golden - this step is what gives real egusi soup its characteristic texture.
Add the tomatoes, jalapeño, ground crayfish, and bouillon, and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the beef and 1 cup water, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach in the last 3 minutes until just wilted.

name: Nigerian Suya Skewers
description: Suya's real spice blend, yaji, is built on real ground roasted peanuts as its backbone - not a spice rub alone - with garlic powder, onion powder, and a bouillon cube rounding out the savory depth that distinguishes true yaji from a generic pepper rub.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

steps_detailed: Mix the ground peanuts with the ginger, paprika, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, and bouillon into a dry rub (yaji).
Toss the sliced beef in the oil, then coat thoroughly in the yaji rub.
Thread onto skewers and grill over high heat, turning, 6-8 minutes, until charred at the edges.

name: Nigerian Pounded Yam
description: Pounded yam, real yam boiled and pounded until smooth and stretchy, is one of Nigeria's most essential starchy staples, traditionally eaten as a smooth accompaniment to soup - real yam is a distinct tuber from sweet potato, with a starchier, firmer texture, and the pounding itself (traditionally by mortar and pestle) is what builds the real elastic, stretchy consistency.

ingredients_full.note: peeled and cubed, white yam is the traditional variety

ingredients.note: peeled and cubed, white yam is the traditional variety

steps_detailed: Boil the yam in salted water 20-25 minutes until completely fork-tender - a knife should slide in with no resistance at all.
Drain well and return the yam to the hot, dry pot for a minute, shaking gently, to steam off excess moisture (this keeps the final texture from turning gummy).

Pound or mash vigorously and continuously until smooth, stretchy, and completely free of lumps - a mortar and pestle gives the real, elastic texture, since the pounding motion itself develops the starches; a sturdy masher worked with real, sustained force is the closest home approximation.
Shape into a smooth dome or individual portions using wet hands, which keeps the surface glossy and prevents sticking.

name: Nigerian Moin Moin
description: Moin moin, a steamed bean pudding, gets its real body from black-eyed peas blended completely smooth with their skins removed - traditionally steamed wrapped in banana leaves or uma leaves, which perfume the pudding as it cooks, though foil or ramekins are the common home approximation. A whole hard-boiled egg or two pressed into the center is a real, traditional addition, not a garnish.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Blend the cowpeas, bell pepper, and onion with a little water into a completely smooth, thick batter - real moin moin has no lumps.
Whisk in the raw egg, palm oil, and bouillon.
Pour into small heatproof cups or ramekins, and press half a hard-boiled egg into the center of each.
Steam over simmering water 35-40 minutes until firm and set all the way through.

name: Nigerian Akara
description: Akara, fried black-eyed pea fritters, depends on real peeled beans blended smooth and then whipped hard by hand before frying - this whipping step works air into the batter, which is what makes real akara light and fluffy inside rather than dense, and it's not optional.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Blend the cowpeas with the onion and jalapeño and a small splash of water into a thick, smooth batter - it should hold peaks, not be runny.
Whip the batter vigorously by hand or with a whisk for several minutes to work air into it - real akara depends on this step for its light interior.
Stir in the bouillon just before frying.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, turning, 4-5 minutes per batch, until deeply golden and cooked through.

name: Nigerian Efo Riro
description: Efo riro depends on the same real fried-down tomato-pepper base as jollof, built in real palm oil, with a generous hand of leafy greens - traditionally a mix of two or more vegetables together, not just one.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

ingredients.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

Brown the beef with the remaining onion, 6-7 minutes, in the palm oil.
Add the blended puree, crayfish, and bouillon, and simmer 12-15 minutes until it reduces and deepens in color.

name: Nigerian Pepper Soup
description: Real Nigerian pepper soup gets its distinctive warmth from a specific spice blend built on uziza seeds, calabash nutmeg (ehuru), alligator pepper, and grains of selim - none of these are distinct items here, so this leans on cumin, ground cloves, and black pepper for a reasonable approximation of the same warm, peppery character, though it honestly lacks their real earthy, slightly bitter complexity. Real crayfish is included since it's genuinely part of the blend, not an optional extra.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

ingredients.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

steps_detailed: Season the chicken with a pinch of salt and set aside 10 minutes.
Combine the chicken, broth, jalapeño, ginger, garlic, and onion in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add the cumin, cloves, black pepper, ground crayfish, and bouillon.
Reduce heat and simmer uncovered 25-30 minutes, so the broth reduces slightly and the spices infuse fully, until the chicken is very tender.
Taste and adjust the pepper level before serving hot.

name: Nigerian Ofada Rice with Ayamase
description: Ayamase, also called designer stew, is a green-pepper stew whose real character comes from a long, patient fry of the blended peppers in oil until they mellow and darken - rushing this step is the most common way to get it wrong. Ofada rice is a specific local Nigerian variety; basmati stands in here as a reasonable but distinct substitute.
steps_detailed: Blend the green bell pepper and jalapeño into a coarse puree.
Heat the palm oil until quite hot and fry the pepper puree, stirring often, 15-18 minutes, until it darkens and mellows - real ayamase depends on this long fry to tame the raw pepper bite.
Add the onion, beef, and bouillon, and cook 8-9 minutes until the beef is browned through.
Cook the rice separately and serve the stew over it.

name: Nigerian Puff Puff
description: Real puff puff is yeast-leavened, which is what gives it a light, slightly tangy character and true puffed shape - yeast isn't a distinct item here, so baking powder stands in for a faster, less complex rise, missing the real tang fermentation would add.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, sugar, and baking powder with warm water into a thick, smooth batter.
Let sit 10-15 minutes to hydrate.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, turning, 4-5 minutes per batch, until deeply golden.

name: Nigerian Chin Chin
description: Chin chin's real crunch comes from a firm, only lightly sweetened dough rolled and cut before frying - real chin chin is closer to a fried biscuit than a doughnut, dense and crisp rather than airy.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, sugar, butter, egg, and nutmeg into a firm dough - it should be stiff, not soft.
Roll out to about 0.5cm thick and cut into small squares or strips.
Fry in batches, turning, 4-5 minutes, until deeply golden and crunchy all the way through.

name: Nigerian Meat Pie
description: The Nigerian meat pie's filling is real curry-forward, distinguishing it from other countries' meat pies - real curry powder and thyme are what give it its distinct, savory character, alongside diced carrot and potato bound into the filling.
steps_detailed: Cut the butter into the flour with a splash of cold water until it forms a firm dough. Chill 20 minutes.
Brown the beef with the carrot, potato, curry powder, thyme, and bouillon, 8-9 minutes, until the vegetables are just tender.
Roll out the dough and cut into rounds, spoon the filling onto one half of each round, fold over, and crimp the edges to seal.
Brush with the egg wash and bake at 375F (190C) for 25-28 minutes until deeply golden.

name: Nigerian Fried Rice
description: Nigerian fried rice is colored and flavored with real curry powder and a real mix of finely diced vegetables - it's distinctly different from Chinese-style fried rice, and is often served alongside jollof rice at the same party table as a matched pair.
steps_detailed: Heat the oil and stir-fry the carrot, green beans, and bell pepper 4-5 minutes.
Add the curry powder and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the cold rice, chicken, and bouillon, and stir-fry over high heat 5-6 minutes, breaking up clumps, until everything is well coated and heated through.

name: Nigerian Fish Stew
description: A tomato-pepper fish stew, built on the same real fried-down base as jollof and efo riro, cooked in real palm oil - a common Nigerian home-cooking staple, real versions often finished with a handful of ground crayfish for extra depth.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

ingredients.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

Fry the onion in the palm oil 3-4 minutes, then add the puree, bouillon, and crayfish, and simmer 15 minutes until it deepens in color and thickens.
Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes until just cooked through, spooning the sauce over it occasionally.

name: Nigerian Dodo (Fried Plantain)
description: Dodo, ripe plantain sliced and fried until caramelized, is a beloved Nigerian side dish, especially alongside jollof rice or beans - the plantain must be genuinely ripe, with a peel that's mostly or fully black, since underripe plantain fries starchy and bland rather than caramelizing into the real sweet, custardy dodo texture. A light dusting of salt right out of the pan, and sometimes a pinch of chili for a spicier dodo ata, is real, common practice.

ingredients_full.note: sliced diagonally, very ripe, peel mostly or fully black

ingredients.note: sliced diagonally, very ripe, peel mostly or fully black

steps_detailed: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Fry the plantain slices in a single layer, without crowding the pan, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply caramelized and golden-brown at the edges.
Drain briefly on paper towels and season immediately with the salt while still hot, so it sticks.

name: Nigerian Okra Soup
description: Okra soup is thickened naturally by okra's own sliminess rather than a starch - real technique keeps some pieces larger for texture, adding the okra toward the end so it doesn't overcook into mush, and real crayfish rounds out the depth alongside the beef.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

ingredients.ingredient: Crustaceans, crayfish, mixed species, farmed, cooked, moist heat

steps_detailed: Brown the beef in the palm oil, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, crayfish, and bouillon, and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Add the okra and simmer 6-8 minutes until just tender - the soup should thicken naturally from the okra itself without turning mushy.

name: Nigerian Coleslaw
description: Nigerian party coleslaw, a mayonnaise-dressed cabbage and vegetable salad, is a fixture at Nigerian parties and celebrations, almost always served alongside jollof rice - real versions typically include a touch of mustard and sugar for real balance against the mayonnaise's richness, not just cabbage and carrot alone.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peas, green, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peas, green, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, and sugar together until smooth.
Toss the cabbage, carrot, and peas with the dressing until every piece is well coated.
Chill at least 20 minutes before serving to let the flavors settle.

name: Nigerian Zobo Drink
description: Zobo, a hibiscus drink, is a beloved Nigerian non-alcoholic beverage, real versions often flavored with real ginger and pineapple, sometimes cloves - not just plain sweetened hibiscus.
steps_detailed: Warm the hibiscus tea with the ginger and cloves 5-6 minutes to infuse.
Stir in the sugar until fully dissolved, then chill completely.
Serve cold over ice with the pineapple chunks stirred through.

name: Nigerian Groundnut Soup
description: Groundnut soup, built on real ground peanuts, is one of Nigeria's most beloved soups, traditionally served with fufu or rice, real versions often finished with a splash of palm oil for a genuine sheen and extra depth.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

Whisk the ground peanuts with 1.5 cups water into a smooth paste.
Add the peanut paste, tomatoes, jalapeño, palm oil, and bouillon to the chicken, and simmer 20-25 minutes until thickened and the chicken is tender.

name: Nigerian Tomato Pepper Base Sauce
description: The foundational fried-down tomato-pepper base that underlies jollof rice, efo riro, ayamase, and many other Nigerian stews, made here on its own for use in other dishes - the real, patient fry is what separates this from a quick tomato sauce.
